definitions.explanation: The feeling of sadness and reluctance when saying goodbye to someone. A literary and formal word.

examples.japanese: {惜別|せきべつ}の{念|ねん}を{抱|いだ}いた。
examples.english: I felt the sadness of parting.

examples.japanese: {恩師|おんし}との{惜別|せきべつ}の{会|かい}が{開|ひら}かれた。
examples.english: A farewell gathering for our mentor was held.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}のホームで{惜別|せきべつ}の{涙|なみだ}を{流|なが}しながら、{友人|ゆうじん}を{見送|みおく}った。
examples.english: I saw my friend off at the station platform, shedding tears of reluctant farewell.

notes:
A literary word expressing sorrow at parting. Composed of {惜|せき} (to regret, to feel reluctant) + {別|べつ} (separation). Used in formal writing, speeches, and literary contexts rather than everyday conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {惜別|せきべつ}の{念|ねん}: feelings of reluctant parting
- {惜別|せきべつ}の{涙|なみだ}: tears of farewell
- {惜別|せきべつ}の{情|じょう}: sentiments of parting
- {惜別|せきべつ}の{会|かい}: farewell gathering
- {惜別|せきべつ}の{辞|じ}: farewell words

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {別|わか}れ: parting, farewell — the most common everyday word
- {送別|そうべつ}: seeing someone off, farewell — focuses on the act of sending off ({送別会|そうべつかい}: farewell party)
- {離別|りべつ}: separation, parting — more neutral; can imply permanent separation
- {告別|こくべつ}: formal farewell — often used for funerals ({告別式|こくべつしき}: funeral ceremony)

REGISTER:
This is a literary and formal word. In everyday speech, {別|わか}れ or {別|わか}れを{惜|お}しむ (to be reluctant to part) is more natural.
